system: Ray versus sphere and capsule primitives
what: Pure maths that returns the distance at which a ray first touches a sphere or a capsule, or -1 for a miss. A ray that starts inside the sphere returns 0. The capsule test falls back to its end spheres when the hit lands beyond the segment.
where: shamble-core.js:1484 raySphere(ox..dz,cx,cy,cz,r); :1485 rayCapsule(ox..dz,ax..az,bx..bz,r) (closed-form infinite-cylinder test plus end-cap spheres; when the ray is parallel to the capsule axis, or the axis has zero length, it falls back to the two end spheres). Only callers: resolveShot core:1498, :1500, :1502.
evidence: none recorded in any report. No report tests these two primitives on their own. The B7 parity test (reports/2026-10-15-team-prep-fixes.md:58) covers statics only. Node check on the real code (core:1484-1485 extracted): a horizontal ray that starts inside the torso cylinder (0,1.2,0) returns -1, a ray that starts inside the head sphere returns 0, and a vertical ray takes the end-sphere fallback. So a muzzle inside another soldier's torso misses that torso. The in-game effect is not measured.
v2_note: Keep the closed-form tests: they are small, allocation-free and easy to port. Fix the inside-start case so the capsule behaves like the sphere (a hit at t=0), and add unit tests with exact cases, which legacy never had. These tests need the same results on Wasm and native, so pick f32 or f64 once and test against the same fixtures on both.
reason: Hit maths the authoritative v2 simulation decides.

system: Ray versus box: axis-aligned and rotated about Y (rayAabb, rayStatic)
what: The slab test returns the hit distance and face normal of a ray against an axis-aligned box. A wrapper handles boxes rotated about the vertical axis (the editor's 45-degree pieces): it turns the ray into the box's frame and turns the normal back.

The 77.7 KB per call is a V8 boxing artefact and goes away in Rust, but the preview should still call the batch query, not loop one box at a time. VISION_V2 §6.2 (a true 3D sim with ledges, interiors and line of sight across heights) and EDITOR_V2 (plateaus and ramps) will need slopes, and maybe full 3D rotation. Ramps are still boxes in the legacy SIM (STATUS.md:90, 'ramps as slopes in SIM' queued). reason: Collision and shot maths the authoritative sim owns.

system: Batch ray versus all static colliders (rayStatics)
what: One loop tests a ray against every live static box (axis-aligned or rotated), with the slab test written inline. It returns the nearest hit closer than a maximum distance, or with anyHit the first one found, and writes the normal and distance into a reused array. A NaN ray counts as blocked only when maxT is NaN as well (as in hasLOS with a NaN end point, and only if at least one live static exists); with a finite maxT, a NaN ray misses everything.

reason: Shot and line-of-sight queries that the authoritative sim decides.

what: A pure query that never changes the world. It casts a shot ray against every live soldier (head, torso and legs), skipping the shooter and, unless friendly fire is on, the shooter's team. Then it tests the static colliders and a flat ground plane, and returns the nearest hit: point, normal, kind, id and body part. The result object is reused on every call. The result record is the contract between the SIM and the game: t, hit point (px, py, pz), unit normal (nx, ny, nz), kind, id, part and mult. kind is one of none, enemy (any soldier, teammates included), building, harvester or block (the ground plane and every other static: crates, walls, platforms, ramps, houses, cover, trees and props). id is the SOLDIERS slot for enemy, the buildings[] index for building, the harvesters[] index for harvester, and -1 for block and none. The game maps a hit back by kind and id (SOLDIERS[r.id], buildings[r.id], harvesters[r.id]) and re-checks team there.

Callers: shamble-game.js:1126 (updateAim hover query), 1309 (_jugFirePilot, Juggernaut), 1489 (castShot), 1625 (enemyFire via _botFireWorld, game:1610), 2869 (torque-bow bolts in update()). Team filter: teamFilter at shamble-game.js:519 (null while TUNE.ff). Result record: pooled at core:1494, fields written at core:1509, ground hit kind='block', id=-1 at core:1507. The ids are set by syncSimWorld: soldier slots game:1446-1448, building id=i game:1450, block id=-1 game:1451 (and 1454-1460), harvester id=i game:1453. Consumers that map kind and id back: game:1128-1133 (updateAim), 1312-1313 (_jugFirePilot), 1493-1495 (castShot), 2870-2871 (bolts).

AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md:25: resolveShot was 13 % of the original ~8 MB/s GC churn. AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md:111: about 1.5 KB per call even when every ray misses (before B7). TECHNICAL.md:90-91 [verified].
v2_note: Keep the pure, read-only design. The comment at core:1491-1492 says it exists so the server can run it against a rewound snapshot for lag compensation, but no rewind is built. Keep one hit world for every shooter (STATUS.md:68, K1). Today bots use _botFireWorld, a view without ramp slots, until ramps become slopes. Keep the team filter, but the server must repeat the team allow-list (STATUS.md:68). Known gaps: the ground is one flat plane (VISION_V2 §6.2 wants a true 3D world with ledges and interiors); kind is 'enemy' for any soldier hit, teammates included when friendly fire is on; only players are swept, with no broad phase (5.4 KB per shot at 48 in JS). How the aim ray is made at height is LOOP_V2 §9 [OPEN]. Keep the idea of a small typed hit result, but make kind an enum and give every static a stable entity id: today every block is id -1, so a hit cannot name which crate, wall or prop it struck, which destructible pieces and replicated hit events will need.
reason: Server-authoritative shot resolution, core of the v2 sim. The aim-at-height input rule is pending LOOP_V2 [OPEN] (§9).

what: A single global object holds the hit world: a list of player records (id, position, alive, stance, team), a list of static colliders (kind, id, alive, box bounds, optional rotation) and a ground height. The game rebuilds it from the live Three.js scene, normally at most once per sim step before shots (frame guard, game:1444). Forced re-syncs come after the player's movement, before the bolts (game:2862), after roster changes (invalidation, game:778), and from the editor's cover-map overlay (shamble-editor.js:564).

reason: The world state the authoritative sim owns; keep the schema and drop the scene-mirror bridge and the global.

what: Answers whether two points can see each other. It casts a segment between them against the static colliders only (soldiers never block) and stops 0.5 m short of the target. The first hit found counts as blocked.
where: shamble-core.js:1544 hasLOS(a,b) (reads the global SIM.statics; calls rayStatics with anyHit=true and maxT=dist-0.5). Callers: bot target acquisition at shamble-game.js:1588 and :1595 (eyes at y+1.45), editor cover-map overlay at shamble-editor.js:574 (START_HERE.md:69 says 565, so the doc has drifted).

v2_note: Keep it as a sim query: bots and the server decide on it. Take the world as an argument instead of reading a global. VISION_V2 §6.2 asks for line of sight across heights and through interiors, so ramps must be slopes, not boxes. Decide explicitly whether units and vehicles block sight; today they do not. The fixed 0.5 m end margin is a tuning value, so it belongs in the data table. Bot use at 48+ players needs the broad phase noted in CS6.
reason: Line of sight is part of bot behaviour and the authoritative sim.

what: Two one-line helpers that return the length of a 2D or 3D vector with a square root. They replaced Math.hypot, which allocates in V8, across the hot paths.
where: shamble-core.js:743 hyp2(a,b), :744 hyp3(a,b,c), outside the fence but used inside it at core:1508 and core:1544. Used on 2 more core lines (323, 876) and 21 game lines (grep by line); the editor was not converted and still has 9 Math.hypot calls.
evidence: AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md:71-72 (CS2): all 25 Math.hypot calls in core and game were rewritten to hyp2/hyp3 by AST, and allocation fell from 8.0 to about 6.3 MB/s (A/B, noise +/-0.5). AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md:25 (P1): Math.hypot was 12.5 % of the original GC churn (the code comment at core:741 calls it 'the #1 source', but the audit puts updateOcclusion and updateSoldierAnim higher at 17 %).
v2_note: In Rust use the vector type's length (no allocation question). Lesson for the TypeScript client: Math.hypot allocated in V8 hot paths here, so measure it before using it per frame. Avoid unguarded sqrt of NaN: a NaN length makes hasLOS's maxT NaN, which rayStatics then reports as blocked (if any live static exists), while a NaN direction with a finite range silently misses.
reason: A V8-only workaround; Rust has native vector lengths, and the TS client just needs the lesson.

what: A comment fence marks the bottom of core as a pure maths block with no THREE or DOM use, kept contiguous so it can be lifted out whole for a later headless simulation (Phase 6). The file header and MODULE_MAP point to it. The block is in fact free of THREE and DOM, but it is not self-contained: BODY reads CHAR_DEFAULT from the character recipe higher up in core, resolveShot and hasLOS call hyp3 from outside the fence, hasLOS reads the global SIM instead of taking the world as an argument, and the VIEW-to-SIM bridge comment and the SIM global sit inside the fenced range. The two lists of what the fence holds disagree: the core header omits rayStatic and rayStatics, MODULE_MAP omits BTN and makeInputCommand.
where: shamble-core.js:1474-1478 fence header ('HEADLESS SIM MATH (pure: zero THREE/DOM)', Phase-6 lift-out target); :1512-1515 VIEW <-> SIM adapter comment and :1516 SIM inside the fenced range; file header pointer core:18-20 (list of fenced symbols) and core:25-26 (not headless-runnable today); docs/MODULE_MAP.md:120-124. Dependencies that cross the fence: core:1482 BODY={...CHAR_DEFAULT.hit} (CHAR_DEFAULT at core:421), hyp3 core:744 used at core:1508 and :1544, hasLOS core:1544 reads SIM.statics.
evidence: none recorded (no report measures or tests the fence). Code read: a grep of core:1474-1544 for THREE, document, window, Math.random, performance and Date finds only the two comment lines that name THREE, so the block is pure of THREE and DOM. MODULE_MAP.md:122-124 states core is not headless-runnable today and that the lift-out is future work.
v2_note: Keep the idea: the simulation lives behind a hard boundary that has no rendering or browser dependency, so the same code runs in the browser and on the server. In v2 that boundary is the Rust simulation crate compiled to Wasm and native (V2_PHASE0_BRIEF.md:7 and :121, R1; repository layout as a Cargo workspace, :125, R5), enforced by the compiler instead of a comment. Learn from the leaks here: shape data (BODY) came from the visual recipe, helpers came from outside the block, and one query read a global. In v2 the sim owns its own data and every query takes the world as an argument. The JS lift-out itself is not worth doing.
reason: A comment convention for a JavaScript lift-out that v2 replaces with the Rust simulation crate boundary; the contents are marked row by row (CS1-CS10).
